text:
Anna R: Ran a focused nsys + perfetto capture on the staging cluster after the Q2 rollout. Seeing one kernel consume a surprising % of GPU time on long sequences: attn_kv_prefetch_v2. attaching a terse summary below.
Mike L: can you paste the top kernels from the trace (time % / SM util)?
Anna R: sure — grabbed the condensed nsys top list:```
attn_kv_prefetch_v2    46.3%   SM util 79.2   warp_idle 20.1
softmax_dropout_fwd     12.5%   SM util 63.0   warp_idle 33.5
layernorm_fwd           9.0%    SM util 58.4   warp_idle 36.9
kv_lookup_async         7.8%    SM util 45.1   warp_idle 49.2
matmul_attn_qkv         6.1%    SM util 81.5   warp_idle 18.0
```
Anna R: note the weird shape: the prefetch kernel is high time but not blocked by low SM util — looks like wavefront / slot contention rather than pure occupancy.
Jared P: hmm. Could be batching window increase -> more parallel KV prefetches colliding on the same SM set. Did you correlate with batch size distribution?
Anna R: yes, the rollout changed the dynamic batcher threshold for short sequences (now triggers later). In the capture the median batch size for long seqs moved from 2->5 which increases simultaneous prefetches.
Sasha K: @Anna R can you rerun a short trace with kv cache disabled (to check pure bandwidth vs contention)?
Anna R: did that quickly — disabling KV cache reduces attn_kv_prefetch_v2 time by ~30% but matmul and qkv climb slightly. So prefetch is doing extra work when cache misses spike.
Devon: sounds like a combo: higher batch parallelism + cache eviction thrash -> prefetch kernel spins longer waiting on memory or doing retries. Can we get a perfetto GPU timeline screenshot (schedules + kernel overlaps)?
Anna R: uploaded timeline to the perf bucket. perf-bot: Trace uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/traces/1734123456/trace.nsctx -> perf-bot
Mike L: proposal: compute a "prominence index" = kernel_time_pct * (1 + warp_idle_pct/100) to rank candidates that consume time while showing high idle. If we sort by that, attn_kv_prefetch_v2 still top.
Jared P: +1. Also stream a sampled nvprof with nvtx markers around batch boundary to see if prefetches are serialized per-stream or truly concurrent.
Anna R: nvprof snippet (sample):```
Kernel: attn_kv_prefetch_v2   samples  1200  avg_time  0.84ms  concurrency_hint: many windows overlap
```
Sasha K: action items: 1) run a narrow replay with batch window=4ms and with/without kv-cache to isolate effect (Anna); 2) collect perfetto CPU->GPU scheduling view and annotate hot SMs (Mike); 3) try a quick micro-optim: serialize prefetch per-SM group via a lightweight stripe allocator to reduce slot contention and measure (Jared); 4) build a small benchmark that reports prominence-index per-kernel per-config (Devon).
Devon: I can wire up the benchmark harness; will add a flag to emit prominence-index CSV and a tiny flamegraph json.
Anna R: ran the narrow replay (batch window 4ms) — attn_kv_prefetch_v2 drops from 46%->28% of GPU time, but overall latency tail increases slightly for short seqs. So it's a knob tradeoff.
Mike L: interesting. We should consider adaptive batch window: shrink when KV miss rate > X or when prominence-index for prefetch > Y.
Jared P: for the kernel-side fix, I sketched a patch to split large prefetch requests into per-SM micro-batches. Small risk but could reduce slot crowding.
Anna R: sharing initial patch in the PR: https://git.redwood.ai/p/eng/runtime/prefetch-stripe (will post results soon).
perf-bot: CI profile run scheduled: job/1734123456-prefetch-stripe-run -> perf-bot
Sasha K: thanks team. quick note — add a unit test under inference/bench/longseq/kv_prefetch_case so we don't regress back to the old batch-window default.
Mike L: ack. I'll add a monitor in the Console that computes prominence-index over the 95th percentile traces nightly. :eyes:
Anna R: thanks. I'll push the narrow-replay traces and the annotated perfetto links into the ticket (ENG-8721).
Devon: leaving a TODO to compute cost delta (tokens/sec) for adaptive-window vs stripe allocator.
Jared P: +1. if stripe reduces peak memory pressure we might also enable a higher quantization path safely. :thumbsup:
Anna R: closing loop for now — will report back after the CI profile and the stripe microbench.
Mike L: thanks, great investigative work.
